# Chapter 13: Peaceful Practices

<margin>K 275</margin>
N 180
W 235

Then the Bodhisattva-Mahasattva <note>a being dedicated to awakening for the benefit of all</note> Manjushri said to the Blessed One, "Blessed One, it is difficult, truly difficult, for these Bodhisattvas-Mahasattvas to persevere out of reverence for the Blessed One. Blessed One, how should these Bodhisattvas-Mahasattvas expound this discourse on the Dharma <term>dharma-paryaya</term> <gloss>teaching or discourse on the Law</gloss> in the future age, in the final time?" 

Upon these words, the Blessed One said to the Bodhisattva Manjushri, "Manjushri, a Bodhisattva-Mahasattva should expound this discourse on the Dharma in the future age, in the final time, by establishing himself in four types of practices. What are these four? Here, Manjushri, a Bodhisattva-Mahasattva should expound this discourse on the Dharma in the future age, in the final time, by establishing himself in proper conduct and proper spheres of association <term>achara-gochara</term> <gloss>behavior and environment</gloss>. 

And how, Manjushri, is a Bodhisattva-Mahasattva established in proper conduct? When, Manjushri, a Bodhisattva-Mahasattva is patient, disciplined, having reached the stage of the disciplined, with a mind that is fearless and unagitated, free from envy. When, Manjushri, a Bodhisattva-Mahasattva does not linger in any conditioned state, and observes the true nature of phenomena as they really are. This lack of discursive thought and lack of conceptualization regarding these phenomena, Manjushri, is called the conduct of the Bodhisattva-Mahasattva. 

<margin>K 276</margin>
W 236

And what, Manjushri, is the sphere of association of a Bodhisattva-Mahasattva? When, Manjushri, a Bodhisattva-Mahasattva does not associate with kings, does not associate with princes, does not associate with high ministers of the king, does not associate with royal officials, does not serve them, does not frequent them, does not approach them. Nor does he associate with other sectarians, wandering ascetics, mendicants, or Jains <term>nirgrantha</term> <gloss>those free from knots/bonds</gloss>, nor with those devoted to secular poetry and treatises. He does not associate with them, does not serve them, does not frequent them, nor does he cultivate friendship with them. 

He does not associate with those who practice the occult, nor with materialists, nor does he serve, frequent, or cultivate friendship with them. He does not associate with outcastes, butchers, pork-sellers, poultry-farmers, hunters, fishmongers, dancers, performers, wrestlers, or pugilists. He does not visit the places of base amusements of others. He does not cultivate friendship with them. If they happen to come to him, he teaches them the Dharma from time to time, but he does so without relying upon them. He does not associate with monks, nuns, laymen, or laywomen who follow the path of the disciples <term>shravaka-yana</term> <gloss>the vehicle of the listeners/disciples</gloss>. He does not serve, frequent, or cultivate friendship with them, nor does he enter into discussion with them, whether in walking meditation or in the monastery. If they happen to come to him, he teaches them the Dharma from time to time, but he does so without relying upon them. This, Manjushri, is the sphere of association of a Bodhisattva-Mahasattva. 

<margin>K 277</margin>

Furthermore, Manjushri, a Bodhisattva-Mahasattva does not teach the Dharma to women by seizing upon any particular signs of attachment, nor does he desire to see them frequently. He does not visit families, nor does he consider that a young girl, a maiden, or a bride should be addressed frequently; he does not engage in casual conversation with them. He does not teach the Dharma to eunuchs, nor does he cultivate friendship with them, nor does he engage in casual conversation with them. He does not enter a house alone for the sake of alms, unless he is contemplating the recollection of the Tathagata <term>tathagata-anusmrti</term> <gloss>mindfulness of the Thus-Come One</gloss>. If he does teach the Dharma to women, he does not do so with a mind of attachment.

<summary>This passage defines the "peaceful practices" of a Bodhisattva, specifically focusing on the disciplined conduct and the restricted social spheres necessary for expounding the Lotus Sutra in difficult, future times.</summary>
<keywords>Manjushri, Bodhisattva, Dharma-paryaya, Conduct, Sphere of Association, Tathagata-anusmrti, Peaceful Practices</keywords>
